title: Update on Application Made against Attorney-General by 17 Prisoners Awaiting Capital Punishment
what_it_is: Update on Application Made against Attorney-General by 17 Prisoners Awaiting Capital Punishment

sections.label: Malay ethnicity drug prosecution challenge
sections.summary: The High Court dismissed the plaintiffs' application alleging the Attorney-General acted arbitrarily and discriminated against them as persons of Malay ethnicity.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim) (for the Minister for Home Affairs)
sentences.text: The application sought declarations that in prosecuting them for capital drug offences, the Attorney-General had acted arbitrarily and discriminated against them as persons of Malay ethnicity and had exceeded his powers and acted unlawfully.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim) (for the Minister for Home Affairs)
sentences.text: On 2 December 2021, the High Court dismissed their application, finding the plaintiffs' allegations to be baseless.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim) (for the Minister for Home Affairs)
sentences.text: The High Court went further to find that the application was an abuse of court process.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim) (for the Minister for Home Affairs)
sentences.text: No appeal was filed against the dismissal of the application.

sections.label: Cause papers given to foreign lawyers
sections.summary: The plaintiffs' counsel breached the Supreme Court Practice Directions by furnishing cause papers, including the affidavit, to foreign lawyers from Lawyers for Liberty.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim) (for the Minister for Home Affairs)
sentences.text: This was a breach of the Supreme Court Practice Directions.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim) (for the Minister for Home Affairs)
sentences.text: It was also revealed that the plaintiffs’ counsel had furnished the cause papers, including the affidavit, to a group of foreign lawyers from a Malaysian human rights NGO, Lawyers for Liberty (LFL).

sections.label: High Court on speculative assertions
sections.summary: The High Court described the allegations as speculative assertions and conjecture cloaked in general interest.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim) (for the Minister for Home Affairs)
sentences.text: The High Court said that the allegations were "speculative assertions" and "conjecture cloaked in general interest".

sections.label: LFL dismissed for no locus standi
sections.summary: The Court dismissed the attempt because LFL had no locus standi.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim) (for the Minister for Home Affairs)
sentences.text: The Court dismissed this attempt as LFL had no locus standi.

sections.label: Foreign interference and public opinion
sections.summary: The passage states they used baseless accusations on race to mobilise public opinion and weaken trust in the criminal justice system.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim) (for the Minister for Home Affairs)
sentences.text: In the incident I referred to, we see them trying to mobilise public opinions, using baseless accusations to play up the issue of race – to weaken Singaporeans’ trust and confidence in our criminal justice system.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim) (for the Minister for Home Affairs)
sentences.text: We must be on our guard against such foreign interference.
